1. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the claimant arising out of the award dated 10.04.2013 passed by IIIrd Additional Member, M.A.C.T., Guna in Claim Case No.45/2012 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation as well as aggrieved by the finding of Claims Tribunal that Insurance Company was totally exonerated from its liability.
2. The date of accident and negligence are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard is not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal in the case of injury received by claimant- Prakash Yadav, Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.21,950/- with interest from the date of filing of claim application till its realization.
4. Learned counsel for the claimant submitted that Claims Tribunal has committed error in awarding the compensation amount.

The Claims Tribunal NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:17222 2 MA-745-2013 awarded compensation is on the lower side.

sentences.text: Hence, prayed for enhancement of compensation by setting aside the order of the Claims Tribunal.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prays for dismissal of this appeal.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, it is undisputed that at the time of alleged accident, driver of the offending vehicle has carried driving licence of LMV and offending vehicle was occurred by Bolero Car (Pick Up) bearing Registration No.MP06-GA- 1079.
It is also undisputed that weight of the offending vehicle was less than 7500 Kg.

In the case o f Mukund Dewagan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. AIR 2017 SC 3668 the Apex Court held that:-
"(ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg. would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

entities.text: Mukund Dewagan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. AIR 2017 SC 3668
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg. or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight"
of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.

A licence issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form"
7.

In view of the aforesaid verdict, at the time of accident, the weight of the offending vehicle was less than 7500 Kg and driver of the offending vehicle NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:17222 3 MA-745-2013 has carried driving licence of LMV.
So, it is clear that no separate endorsement on license is required to drive transport vehicle.
So, findings of the Claims Tribunal in exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability is erroneous and is hereby set aside.
8. Now, heard on the question of enhancement of compensation.

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and more particularly the age of injured and injuries received by him, it shall be appropriate to enhance the amount by Rs.40,000/- in addition to the amount already awarded by Claims Tribunal which shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal in its award from the date of filing of the application.
10. Resultantly, this appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
The insurance company is liable to pay the enhanced amount of Rs.40,000/- to the claimant jointly and severally with owner and driver.
However, first liability is fastened upon the insurance company to pay the compensation amount.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate from the date of filing of the claim application till its realization.
